summary: Vincent Eltschinger works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Collège Saint-Michel and the University of Lausanne, he held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the University of Vienna, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Vincent Goossaert is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology who studied under Kristofer Schipper. He held posts at CNRS, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études as Professor of Daoist History.

Vincent Lefèvre specializes in history/archaeology and Indology. He studied at École Nationale des Chartes, Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and under Bruno Dagens, later serving as a curator at Musée Guimet from around 2002 to 2013.

Vincent Tournier specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at École Pratique des Hautes Études, Leiden University, and under Seishi Karashima, later taking up a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 2018.
Vincenzo Vergiani specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Raffaele Torella and held a post at the University of Cambridge around 2009.

Virendra Nath Misra worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University from around 1958 to 1961 and served as Director of Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from around 1993 to 2000.
Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar was an Indologist who studied at St John's College, Cambridge (circa 1906–1909) and as a pupil under Heinrich Lüders (circa 1911–1914).
Vishwanath Prasad Varma works in philosophy and Indology. His education included studying under Dhirendra Mohan Datta, Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, doctoral supervisor Kalikinkar Datta, and Joachim Wach.
Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who studied under MA supervisor Karin Preisendanz, Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita.

Vladimir L. Uspensky is a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He held posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts as assistant keeper of the Tibetan collection and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Vladimir Tikhonov works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at St. Petersburg University, Korea University, and under Kwang Cho, Chul-hwan Chung, and Mikhail Nikolaevich Pak, later becoming a professor at the University of Oslo.
Volkbert Näther is an Indologist who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg by 1975 under doctoral supervisor Claus Vogel and committee member Wilhelm Rau.

Volker Caumanns specializes in Tibetology, studying at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Ludwig Maximilian University under Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He held posts at Munich, Lumbini International Research Institute, and the University of Bern.

Volker Grabowsky is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Kiel. He held positions at the universities of Passau and Hamburg, the National University of Laos, and the University of Münster.
W. F. Jayasuriya worked in the field of Buddhist studies, having studied under teachers Rerukane Ariyaratne, H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.
W. H. D. Rouse was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who received his education at Cheltenham College and Christ's College, Cambridge.

W. H. R. Rivers studied at Tonbridge School, Barts and The London School of Medicine and Dentistry, the University of London, and St John's College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at University College London and the University of Cambridge.

W. Norman Brown specialized in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Hiram College, Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, and with Franklin Edgerton, later serving as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania from roughly 1926 to 1966.

W. Randolph Kloetzli works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under teachers including Mircea Eliade and Paul Tillich, and lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

W. S. Karunaratne specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Dharmaraja College, Ananda College, University of Ceylon, and SOAS University of London, later serving as Dean of the Faculty of Oriental Studies at the University of Ceylon.
